title: simple substring query seems to be impossible with elasticsearch/lucene--please add it.
body: <!-- feature request -->\r   describe the feature  :  \r \r in elasticsearch, it seems impossible to search for an arbitrary substring, perhaps including spaces.  searching for part of a word isn't quite enough; i want to search any substring of an entire field. \r \r suppose i have only a few thousand documents in my elasticsearch index, and i try:\r \r   \ query\ : {\r          \ wildcard\  : { \ description\  : \  plan \  }\r   }\r that works as expected--i get every item where \ plan\  is in the description, even ones like \ supplantation\ .\r \r now, i'd like to do\r \r   \ query\ : {\r          \ wildcard\  : { \ description\  : \  plan is \  }\r   }   \r ...so that i might match documents with \ kaplan isn't\  among many other possibilities.\r \r i was hoping there might be something built-in for this elasticsearch, given that this simple substring search seems like a very basic capability  thinking about it, it is implemented as strstr   in c, like '%%' in sql, ctrl+f in most text editors, string.indexof in c , etc. , but this seems not to be the case. it seems this isn't possible with wildcard, match prefix, or any other query type i might see. how do i simply search on any substring?\r \r i could use a regexp query, but even that is limited to a field that uses the keyword analyzer and is 32k or less.  i also have to convert my term to lowercase, even if the data has uppercase.\r \r  i am aware any such query would be slow or perhaps even impossible for large data sets. \r \r see also https://stackoverflow.com/questions/30379094/elasticsearch-regexp-with-space-not-working\r \r

title: store user id from posted username, rather than hidden input field
body: related: https://github.com/affiliatewp/affiliatewp/issues/1116\r \r affiliatewp provides a popup when searching for an affiliate. if you click an affiliate in the search popup, it stores the affiliate's user id in a hidden input field. this will not correctly store the affiliate's user id in some instances. here's 2:\r \r 1. when the site admin manually types in the affiliate's username, sees the affiliate they want, and finishes off typing without selecting the affiliate from the popup search box.\r \r 2. when there's already an affiliate entered and the site admin deletes it then enters a new username, again without using the affiliate search.\r \r i propose we always work out the user id based on the posted username, and not rely on the user id posted along with the user_id field. this means the user id will be always be correct, when the affiliate username is typed in by the site admin, or the username is selected from the search popup. it's an extra small step but much better imo, unless i'm missing something obvious.

title: optional field with default value not deserialized correctly when value is missing
body: i'm trying to implement schema evolution adding a new field to an existing schema. the new field's schema looks like this:\r    \r {\r     \ name\ : \ useragent\ ,\r     \ type\ :  \r         \ null\ ,\r         \ string\ \r      ,\r     \ default\ : null\r }\r    \r generated case class is correctly initializing the field as  useragent: option string  = none , so new instances of the schema are serialized correctly as:  \ useragent\ :null \r \r the problem arises for old records serialized with the old version of the schema: the field being optional and with a default value should make the record fully forward compatible, but when deserializing the record avro4s assigns the field a default value of  jsonproperties.null_value   that gets converted to string, resulting in in:  some \ org.apache.avro.jsonproperties$null@5300cac\   \r \r as a workaround, i'm overriding the implicit for  optionfromvalue  this way:\r    \r implicit def optionfromvalue t  implicit fromvalue: fromvalue t   = new fromvalue option t   {\r     override def apply value: any, field: field : option t  = value match {\r         case jsonproperties.null_value => none\r         case _ => option value .map  value: any  => fromvalue.apply value  \r     }\r }\r    \r this works, but i guess it should be handled correctly in avro4s.

title: memory is stack allocated with 4096 bytes, which may cause stack overflows.
body: currently the cpu memory is an array  u8 type  with a size of 4096 bytes. this is stack allocated, and stack overflows can become a problem.\r \r > reference:  cpu.rs line 36:\r > \r > pub struct cpu {\r >     opcode: u16,\r >     memory:  u8; 4096 ,                  \r >     v:  u8; 16 ,                        \r >     i: u16,                            \r >     pc: u16,                          \r >     stack:  u16; 16 ,                \r >     sp: u16,                        \r >     delay_timer: u8,               \r >     sound_timer: u8,              \r >     pub draw_flag: bool,         \r >     pub pixels:   bool; 64 ; 32 ,\r >     pub keypad:  u8; 16 ,       \r > }\r > \r \r \r suggestion is to use box  https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/boxed/struct.box.html  for heap allocation. memory can instead be a box that contains a vector.

title: objects should not call  eventbus.register this   in constructors
body: problem\r registering an object to the event bus inside of a constructor call can result in a subscriber being called prior to all of the fields in the class being fully constructed. this can lead to null pointer exceptions for fields that are final and should have been initialized in the classes constructor.\r \r  relavent gitter discussion  https://gitter.im/wpiroboticsprojects/grip?at=564baf1609446b3b7461702a  discovery of problem and discussion of how to fix it.\r \r  guava google groups discussion with dev  https://groups.google.com/forum/ !topic/guava-discuss/4zjhhpmmvkq \r \r >    don't publish the \ this\  reference during construction\r one of the mistakes that can introduce a data race into your class is to expose the this reference to another thread before the constructor has completed. sometimes the reference is explicit, such as directly storing this in a static field or collection, but other times it can be implicit, such as when you publish a reference to an instance of a non-static inner class in a constructor. constructors are not ordinary methods -- they have special semantics for initialization safety. an object is assumed to be in a predictable, consistent state after the constructor has completed, and publishing a reference to an incompletely constructed object is dangerous. listing 2 shows an example of introducing this sort of race condition into a constructor. it may look harmless, but it contains the seeds of serious concurrency problems.\r > \\- brian goetz  http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/library/j-jtp0618/ \r \r   resolution\r this can be resolved by ensuring that constructors never call a register method\r

title: fix reading queryname-sorted input crams with unmapped reads
body: from @cmnbroad:\r \r the write side for non-coordinate sorted crams works now, but there is still a problem with reading queryname sorted input crams with unmapped reads. there is an existing test in gatk for this case that is already enabled and has been passing, but only because there is another bug in the test code that is masking the failure because it uses the value \ outputextension\ , which results in a bam file being created. when i went to fix that as part of re-enabling the disabled cram tests, the verification of the queryname test output now fails. the test itself runs, but the samsequalstringent verification fails reading the output. so the write-side issues with the presorted flag are fixed with samtools/htsjdk 368, but there is still a limitation in htsjdk for reading crams with unmapped reads that are not coordinate sorted that we need to fix/understand.\r \r see also:\r https://github.com/broadinstitute/gatk/issues/777\r https://github.com/samtools/htsjdk/issues/404

title: the future of .mjs
body: so i'm aware this is all still under the experimental flag and recognise its status as a result.\r \r however, a fair amount of discussion is taking place across typescript and babel regarding where to direct attention with regard to modules.\r \r https://github.com/microsoft/typescript/issues/18442\r \r a major point of uncertainty is whether or not the current es modules 'mode' and .mjs will continue on.\r \r for what i can see, it seems like .mjs is here to stay. the goal of having a unified set of functionalites under a single file extension is obviously where you want to go, but .mjs/es mode seems like the 'stepping' stone that will eventually make that a reality.\r \r is it possible to get a confirmation around how .mjs is to be treated, so basic file extension support can be approved with the caveat of it being experimental?\r \r i'm one of i'm guessing many who have run with .mjs based projects, and would love to see a clear directive on this. it's been a long time coming i think.

title: split psp defaulting and validation
body: when authz is added to psp admission  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/33080  the user submitting the request will now be taken into account for psp selection.  that means that if one user creates a pod and another user updates the pod the psp options that the pod validates against may be different.  \r \r since the podspec should not be mutable on the fields that psp defaults anyway the psp logic should be split so that defaulting only occurs during an add operations.  an update operation should only attempt to validate that the user has a psp that would allow the requested spec.\r \r \r ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/33080/files r84148684

title: make dozerbeanmapper immutable. part i. deprecating setters.
body: currently  dozerbeanmapper  allows users to change its configuration after instantiation. this has several drawbacks:\r   encourages users to work with implementation, as  mapper  interface does not provide those \ set\  methods;\r   adds additional logic to synchronize initialization of internals and track that this is done only once.\r \r i assume, these \ set\  methods were introduce to avoid multiple constructors for all possible configuration options. this will not be an issue after fluent builder is introduced in  375.\r \r suggestion:\r   replace \ set\  methods from  dozerbeanmapper  with constructor parameters;\r   add fluent api to configure those parameters in builder created in  375;\r   make   dozerbeanmapper  package-private as users will only use builder and  mapper .\r \r during this implementation some logic is likely to be extracted from  dozerbeanmapper  to the third classes. for instance,  mapper  requires only final mapping config, thus merging xml mappings and java mapping builders is a perfect candidate to be delegated to another class.

title: old 100  auto-update feature with stable/dev channels
body: added by mark liversedge over 2 years ago. updated over 1 year ago.\r description\r --\r it would be very useful to offer a feature to automatically update the goldencheetah binary when new releases are made available. this would mean publishing binaries at a public location and periodically checking for a new version upon startup.\r \r additionally, google chrome offers a 'developer', 'stable' and 'beta' channel to allow brave users to subscribe to latest dev releases. it would be useful if we supported this functionality, especially to allow non-technical users to adopt the latest developer builds between releases.\r \r gareth coco has done an amazing job automating builds for win32, and is looking at linux at the moment. we should exploit these builds  which are public .\r \r i suspect the mechanics of overwriting binaries / dlls may prove to be platform specific, so we could possibly stage this feature and support windows, linux ahead of mac, which is potentially more complex  ? .\r \r \r history\r --\r   1  updated by robb romans over 2 years ago\r  \r this is a cool idea. i might put it behind in priority to having binary builds available in package manager format, such as debs for ubuntu or rpms for red hat and suse, whatever mac uses, and self-installing windows packages. the linux formats can be built from source into debs or rpms with some additional build magic. getting binary builds in a package manager format might be considered a prerequisite to this feature, unless you want to reinvent packaging and distribution. you'd also need someone to periodically build the packages, and a public place to host the binaries.\r \r these are old but informative about the general process:\r create debian linux packages\r http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/linux/library/l-debpkg.html\r \r packaging software with rpm, part 1: building and distributing packages\r http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/library/l-rpm1/index.html\r \r once you have that, for automatic updates, \r fedora, rh: yum repos: http://www.webmo.net/support/yum_repository.html\r ubuntu: ppas: https://help.launchpad.net/packaging/ppa\r mac: ?\r windows: ? title: vector.of   is ambiguous with gwt compiler
body: there are two static methods overloading  vector.of   . one is accepting a single   t element   https://github.com/javaslang/javaslang/blob/21858c024061c1bf1a248d75e01a5b63520e7c26/javaslang/src/main/java/javaslang/collection/vector.java l97 , the other a varargs   t... elements   https://github.com/javaslang/javaslang/blob/21858c024061c1bf1a248d75e01a5b63520e7c26/javaslang/src/main/java/javaslang/collection/vector.java l111 . the gwt compiler creates a method reference to the wrong method   t element  instead of the varargs version  when inferring the method reference from the body of   vector.tabulate   https://github.com/javaslang/javaslang/blob/21858c024061c1bf1a248d75e01a5b63520e7c26/javaslang/src/main/java/javaslang/collection/vector.java l128 . this way, under gwt, the  tabulate  method will create a  vector  of arrays instead of  vector  of  t .\r \r since afaik gwt uses the eclipse compiler, this probably causes problems with older version of eclipse too  haven't tested .\r \r i think it's a bit unfortunate that the two methods share the same name since ambiguity can happen. what if i want a vector of arrays? what if i want a vector of elements of the array. i think renaming the varargs version to  ofall  would make sense and would align it to the other methods which accept either primitive varargs or iterables or streams.\r \r another solution could be to remove the  vector.of t element   version altogether, since the varargs version should be enough, that's what varargs was invented for in the first place.\r \r personally, i like the first  rename  solution more , but the second one  remove  could be backwards source-compatible, while the rename will not.

title: add support for 3-legged oauth for \ native app\  clients to globus auth
body: globus auth is adding a concept of \ native app\  clients which do a full 3-legged oauth flow even though they do not have a client secret.\r doing this flow requires the use of a temporary pkce secret to play the role of a client secret when getting an authorization code.\r \r although support for this flow in the cli   globus/globus-cli 16   is the first target, we should make sure that our bindings are sufficiently generic that they can be used for applications employing other flows.\r in particular, some apps will be using an embedded browser to implement this flow, and supporting that as well as cli use will probably cover the majority of our use cases.\r \r after a discussion with @jaswilli, we reached the conclusion that there's little use for the state parameter passed through the oauth flow, so we don't need to contend with the possibility of multiple simultaneous authentication flows. handling one at a time will be sufficient for the foreseeable future.\r \r @bd4 i think it's desirable for the sdk to encapsulate parts of this flow, as it has to generate a secret, send it, and then send a related secret to exchange the auth code for a token.\r it's nice to think of a client for a given service as your way of \ talking to\  that service, so i think this should be built as a helper hanging off of the  authclient  object.\r \r i'm putting together a proposed structure for this, even though the support for it in globus auth has not yet been released.

title: policy proposal: if you need static types, use typescript
body: following up on @ackernaut's governance on deprecation, i have a simple proposal on types.\r right now, we use js with a few flow files sprinkled in.\r \r personally, i think flow is going the way of draftjs. a better analogy might be that just as graphql is a more powerful version of falcor, typescript is a more powerful version of flow.\r \r i don't think we need to convert the whole project to typescript. in many, many cases, things are really simple. there are only a few cases where objects become very complex & it's nice to get that free static typechecking. the best usecases for it are: \r - it tells me when something could be undefined\r - it tells me when i'm trying to grab a prop from an object that may not have that prop\r - there are so many libraries out there with typings. like all of em, including the dom, which is great, because if i write something like  node.contenttext  it'll tell me that may not exist, so i'll need to first make sure that node is a textnode.\r - when i refactor things, like taking a property out of an object, i get red squiggles all over the project telling me where things were depending on that thing i removed.\r - it self-documents so everything that i can type pops up in intellisense. an examle of the self-documenting docs is here: https://mattkrick.github.io/fast-rtc-peer/classes/fastrtcpeer.html isofferer\r \r i also don't feel bad about waiting this long to do it. v1 was awful. after reading the entire changelog, typescript hit its stride around v2.2 & now at v3.0.1, it's really promising. i recently tried it out with a few side projects, got a good linting config & webpack build strategy for it so adding it into the project should be painless.

title: split project.lock.json into  .lock.json and  .cache.json
body: i've read  this gist on checking in project.lock files  https://gist.github.com/brunomlopes/97b433593d61e5481788  a couple times over and i really feel the current locking design feels optimized for the wrong scenario: finding breaking changes in moving targets.  whereas the more important default scenario should be repeatable builds.  to the best of my understanding the current project.json.lock now serves two purposes, caching the files in play for compilation and optionally locking dependencies  using  --lock .   this results in a bit of a operational kerfuffle. when do i need to restore using  --lock  ? do i need to unignore lock files in release tags, and if so is this not important on dev branch too? if i branch of those tags should i remove the lock file on the first change?   what if locking is simply the norm just as it is in paket?  restore writes a very minimal  project.lock.json   look at  paket for an example  http://fsprojects.github.io/paket/lock-file.html   if not present that you should   always   commit  eradicating both  --lock  and  lock:false  confusion .  when dnx runs the app for the first time it will generate a  .project.cache.json  which you should   never   commit.   if folks want to check fast moving targets on a ci server they could do  dnu restore --latest  on the ci servers explicitly. -  dnu restore --latest  updates all     dependencies -  dnu restore --update  updates all dependencies to latest -  dnu restore --outdated  simply reports on packages that are outdated  to be fair  the wiki  https://github.com/aspnet/home/wiki/lock-file  does not dictate not checking  project.lock.jso n files but does leave it up in the air without a consistent story.  even if we do not make locking the norm a split will really help those who do choose to commit the lock file to not be faced with merge conflicts in the cached files section of this lock file.

title: automatically set environment variables based on working directory
body: environment variables are sometimes used to resolve include paths, indicate which compiler to use, etc. while having a sensible global default i.e. in .config/fish/fish.config works most of the time, some projects will require these envvars to be set to specific values for that application. go and java applications are prime examples gopath and classpath respectively , but other examples also exist, such as projects requiring a particular c compiler e.g. cc=clang .\r \r it would be fantastic if fish could provide a feature that allows me to indicate that a particular subtree in the file system should have some particular set of environment variables. this could be taken to the extreme by allowing a function to be called when a shell enters/leaves a particular directory or any of its children , but a simple approach more akin to vim's localvimrc might be sufficient. if we want to avoid the risk of security problems arising from automatically sourcing potentially untrusted files without resorting to whitelisting/blacklisting, an alternative would be to set per-directory settings in your fish config, but this is a strictly less useful feature.\r \r thoughts?

title: high latencies in grpc requests when going through envoy
body: hi everyone,\r \r we have a grpc client and server service as part of our system, hosted on google cloud kubernetes. between these two are a ingress controller using contour and envoy, and an esp. in our production system, we are observing high latency intervals that come an go. we removed the esp but that did not make a big difference, but when bypassing the envoy proxy, latencies immediately improve. other interesting bits are that the latencies seem to correlate with the request load, although the envoys are pretty idle and the actual traffic is relatively low  ~20rq/s . it also seems that a restart of the client service helps for a while, but after 30min to one hour the problem re-surfaces. it also appears that sometimes there is a 5min \ comb\  structure in the latency pattern\r \r please see the two attached plots, one is with the envoy proxy, one is bypassing it. \ maba\  refers to the client service and \ maus\  to the server. please ignore the red lines, this was an attempt to extract data directly frmo envoy logs that didn't work so well. the solid line on the second page is the 99 percentile. notice how well the \ maba\  latencies envelop the \ maus\  latencies in the \ good\  case, and how disassociated they are when going through envoy?\r \r  leaks-all-over-the-place-and-5min-spikes.pdf  https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/files/2088955/leaks-all-over-the-place-and-5min-spikes.pdf \r  no-envoy-no-esp-good.pdf  https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/files/2088956/no-envoy-no-esp-good.pdf \r \r i appreciate that this issue does not have enough information, but it's a complicated setup and i don't really know where to start. please let me know what further information is required to investigate and resolve this.

title: simplified calibration routines for qubit object.
body: this relates to  42 which deals with the parameter naming.  \r \r in addition to cleaning up the parameter names in the qubit object   42 , we should clean up the calibration functions. the dependency graph based tuning provides some constraints that provide structure to this process. discussions with @fluthi and @cdickel provided some more ideas on this. \r \r i propose the following \r - every distinct calibration step corresponds to a single function in the qubit object\r - every distinct calibration step corresponds to a single node in the dependency graph\r - the calibrate funtions can be called blindly  i.e., without specifying any arguments  and will return either a value indicating it was succesful or a boolean false indicating failure. \r - calibration functions  e.g, find_frequency_spec, calibrate_freq_ramsey  are specified in the qubit_object abstract base class and within them call \ measure_xx\  functions that are specific for different hardware configurations. \r - the interface of every measure_xx function will be specified in the qubit_object abstract base class. \r \r what will change? \r - currently the functions often require specifying some arguments to make it work or encompass multiple different calibrations  e.g. find frequency does both the cw_spec, pulsed_spec and ramsey method . \r      - sensible defaults will be specified\r      - functions will be split up when required. \r \r we will need to argue over what should and should not be included in a calibration to determine what functions will be required. i'd appreciate feedback from everyone as much as possible. \r \r below is an initial graph i'm using now. i'd like some more input on what extras will be required  such as extracting dac arcs, decoupling matrices etc . \r ! image  https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/6142932/26678498/157cb1b6-46d1-11e7-8872-008efc96c9e9.png

title: nic_router: handle uplink link_state
body: we are experiencing the following problem:\r we have a nic_router with some clients and an uplink connected to a nic_drv.\r whenever we plug out the network cable, the network packets are still sent from the router to the driver until the buffer is full. \r when we plug in the cable again, a few packets which were buffered are sent over the wire directly, but any further packets are not sent and the clients are unable to send or receive any messages over the network from then on. only restarting the system or restarting the nic_router seems to fix this.\r \r looking into the code of nic_router, on the uplink side it does not seem to do anything with the link_state and the link_state_sigh. but we think it should do something at least, like sending an icmp 'destination unreachable' packet to the client if it tries to send packets to the uplink, perhaps propagating the link_state signal to the client side, or take some other action. at least the uplink domain should do the dhcp handshake again, as we might have plugged the computer into a different network. we think it should not send old buffered messages over the wire when it gets plugged in again, considering a user might send sensitive data over a public network after it was plugged out from a private network.\r \r another additional nice feature would be to include the link_state in the nic_router report. this way, some other components can know the current network state and act accordingly.

title: unions should build as selects
body: i'm trying to build a tool that goes from some fairly human readable data representation such as json into tightly packed byte arrays. unions are great 1:many mappings of bytes -> structured data, but the implementation in construct isn't very useful for many:1 mappings of structured data -> bytes. take the below code for example:\r \r    \r from construct import  \r \r class quickobj object :\r     def __init__ self,   kwargs :\r         self.__dict__.update kwargs \r \r test_union = union \ test_union\ ,\r     embed struct \ foo\ ,\r         ulint8 \ a\  ,\r         ulint8 \ b\  \r       ,\r     embed struct \ bar\ ,ulint16 \ c\    \r  \r \r test_ok = quickobj a=1,b=2 \r test_union.build test_ok \r test_fail = quickobj c=513 \r test_union.build test_fail \r    \r \r because test_fail doesn't follow the \ foo\  struct, the  .build    fails, which isn't expected behavior because test_fail is a valid form of the many possible structured data representations. this basically forces you to reproduce the union twice; once with construct's  union , and once in your python-side object or an adapter.\r \r i think this could be solved by having  union  .build  behave somewhat like  select  .build . try each subcon in order until one works.

title: convert the static methods and attributes in cloudsim class to instance methods and attributes
body: feature:\r cloudsim class is used just in a static context, since all its methods and attributes are static. by this way, the class stores data related to a particular simulation being run, what makes impossible to run multiple simulations in parallel.\r \r using cloudsim instances will provide a complete isolation between simulations being executed in parallel.\r \r the use of static methods also makes very difficult to test classes that depend on cloudsim class.\r mocking a static method can just be performed using libraries such as powermock, that introduces more complexity to test writing. \r \r    detailed information about how the feature should work\r the static elements in cloudsim class have to be converted to instance elements and the class has to provide public constructors to be used to initialise the simulation, instead of calling a static init method.\r \r    an example scenario where this feature should be used\r it will allow running several simulations in parallel, avoiding that a simulation interfere in the results of other ones. \r \r it will also make much easier to write unit tests for classes that depend on cloudsim, since a simple library such as easymock, that is already being used, can create mock objects without a large increase in tests complexity.\r \r    a brief explanation of why you think this feature is useful\r it will take one step further in moving away from cloudsim issues and paving the way to provide a highly extensible and maintainable framework.\r \r it will allow to write more and meaningful tests to increase framework accuracy and provides the base for inclusion of upcoming features.

title: question  abort segment requests if client bandwidth changes drastically
body: i am working to decrease buffering rates on our applications. it looks like we may need to implement a more advanced abrmanager since shaka player has already configuration that allows to accept a custom abrmanager. however, i am curious about a few points. are you planning to improve abrmanager's ability in the future instead of keeping a simple one?\r \r if you have a plan, let me share a few ideas that i have:\r \r 1. let's say, abrmanager is downloading a segment at 8000kps, then suddenly client bandwidth drops to 1000 kbps. so, abrmanager may abort the request and may request the lowest variant. also, consider vice versa.\r 2. unless i am wrong, shaka retries requests as long as we configure the retry times. let's say, first few requests have failed and i assume shaka would not retry different variant which has a different bitrate. so, what if abrmanager detects this failed requests and lower the bitrate. this would be also valuable if the request timeout exceeds.\r 3. some devices might have performance issues. i specifically work on samsung and lg tvs. those platforms are definitely non-performant and the app can be stuck when the cpu reaches its capacity. so, what if we implement to find/estimate the cpu performance of the device and perform a better variant selection by abrmanager.\r 4. abrmanager can send multiple segment requests by using web workers. since other requests would be made on different thread, it would not make any performance issue on the main thread. so, abrmanager can append available buffers by considering these different responses.\r \r please let me know what your thoughts are on these.\r \r thank you,\r semih.

title: 'prefix separators' are fragile and easily broken.
body: we have a feature that allows a separator to be declared for transparent prefixes.\r \r the relevant code is here:\r \r https://github.com/melt-umn/silver/blob/develop/grammars/silver/modification/copper/prefix.sv\r https://github.com/melt-umn/silver/blob/develop/grammars/silver/modification/copper/parserdcl.sv\r \r the problem is that the discovery of a prefix separator works like this:\r \r https://github.com/melt-umn/silver/blob/develop/grammars/silver/modification/copper/prefix.sv l67\r \r    \r getvaluedcl \ _prefix_seperator\ , top.env \r    \r \r presently, this works in toy examples because either:\r \r 1. there is only one grammar involves that declares a prefix separator.\r 2. the prefix separator is specified as part of the parser declaration, which  erroneously  suppresses new declarations defs from propagating outward.\r \r https://github.com/melt-umn/silver/blob/develop/grammars/silver/modification/copper/parserdcl.sv l20\r \r    \r top.defs =  fundef top.grammarname, n.location, namedsig  ;\r m.env = appendenv toenv liftedagdcls.defs ++ med.defs , top.env ;\r    \r \r here,  liftedagdcls  gets sent back down the parser declaration list   m   and is not included in the general declarations  really, as it should be. \r \r some other, more robust, mechanism is necessary for specifying prefix separators.

title: feature request for rma initiator to prepare remote mr for use
body: this came from the a3cube port of libfabric.  a3cube requires that the initiator of an rma operation 'connect' to the remote memory region.  libfabric does not require this.  the result is that the provider implementation needs to use a connection cache on each rma operation.  one possibility is to add some sort of 'prepare_remote_mr' call that an initiator can call that would replace the mr key provided by the remote side with a mr key usable by the local side.  note that this call may also allow providers a way to support mr keys > 64 bits.  e.g. the providers could use a key exchange protocol to obtain all of the data that's necessary.

body: i use resample often and always find that i always need to go in and manually reset its parameters to be appropriate to the dataset i'm using. for example if i'm working with 2d data, resample comes up with 3d box checked, and i have to uncheck that. also, it does not get the range of the independent variables right. it generally seems to clip things off at the edges and i have to go in and put the min/max values in manually. finally, the resolution  i think the default is 10  for the resampling is always to coarse for the data i'm working with. one usually wants a resolution that's finer than the dataset one is using. could the defaults for resample be made a little more intelligent so that better guesses are made based on the properties of the data stream going into it? this would save the user from having to go in and tweak things each time.      -----------------------redmine migration----------------------- this ticket was migrated from redmine. as such, not all  information was able to be captured in the transition. below is a complete record of the original redmine ticket.  ticket number: 265 status: developer review project: visit tracker: feature priority: normal subject: better initialization for resample assigned to: dave pugmire category:  target version:  author: don spong start: 07/06/2010 due date:  % done: 0 estimated time:  created: 07/06/2010 03:50 pm updated: 07/20/2010 01:23 pm likelihood:  severity:  found in version:  impact: 3 - medium expected use: 4 - common os: all support group: doe/scidac description:  i use resample often and always find that i always need to go in and manually reset its parameters to be appropriate to the dataset i'm using. for example if i'm working with 2d data, resample comes up with 3d box checked, and i have to uncheck that. also, it does not get the range of the independent variables right. it generally seems to clip things off at the edges and i have to go in and put the min/max values in manually. finally, the resolution  i think the default is 10  for the resampling is always to coarse for the data i'm working with. one usually wants a resolution that's finer than the dataset one is using. could the defaults for resample be made a little more intelligent so that better guesses are made based on the properties of the data stream going into it? title: what about depth vs. breadth of experience?
body: going against the grain here.\r \r while pillar places great emphasis on the desirability of being a polyglot, which i think is just fine so far as it goes, my view is that we neglect the value of depth of knowledge in particular areas.  i think we lose the ability to be thought leaders in our industry by emphasizing one so much over the other.\r \r no one has every told me _not_ to go for depth of knowledge, but it feels to me that our culture encourages being a mile wide and an inch deep and does not _actively_ support/emphasize becoming expert in any particular thing.  sure, we can do it on our own and i support that concept of self-motivated growth.  however, if pillar wants to have the _industry/tech stack expert_ arrow in the quiver, we will have to look for ways to encourage and support gaining that knowledge.\r \r we can do a lot on our own, but i don't believe we can do _everything_ on our own.\r \r     how it relates to the guild\r \r a careful reading of our desired behaviors shows no mention of deep expertise.  proficiency is _not_ the same thing as being an expert.  \r \r are we a one-trick pony in this regard?  do we want to be?  these are not criticisms...they are honest questions.  it may well be a case of \ that's not what we do\ .\r \r so, is the only path to advancement to be a really good generalist?

issue may be ignored otherwise                   -->\r <!--- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -->\r <!---  only submit bug reports here. for help or questions to the community -->\r <!---  see the forum: https://foundation.zurb.com/forum                     -->\r \r as reported by @jasonmiller at https://github.com/zurb/foundation-sites/pull/10978 issuecomment-393301646, the new breakpoint precision   0.0001em   introduce a  new bug on all major browsers  chrome, firefox, safari... .\r \r    what should happen?\r \r for the following code:\r    scss\r $breakpoints:  \r   small: 0,\r   medium: 640px,\r   large: 1024px,\r  ;\r \r .test {\r     @include breakpoint medium down  { ... }\r }\r    \r \r properties should be applied for  medium and under , so for a resolution strictly inferior to  1024px .\r \r    what happens instead?\r \r due to the breakpoint  63.99999em  being rounded to  64em  by most browsers for their breakpoint calculations, properties are still applied on the  large  breakpoint for  1024px  exactly.\r \r this issue is related to:\r    10978 fix breakpoints precision issue with a smaller global font size  @jasonmiller \r    10820 show-for   and hide-for   gap at exact width of breakpoint  @lazerproof \r    10695 'show-for-small-only' and 'hide-for-small-only' elements both displaying at a certain width  @hofuchi \r \r    possible solution\r <!--- not obligatory, but suggest a fix/reason for the bug,                 -->\r <!--- or ideas how to implement the addition or change.                     -->\r \r as seen in  10978, we need a subpixel precision to handle zoomed browsers. but browsers handle sub-pixel mediaqueries badly and a too high precision causes the issue described above. so we have to find the proper balance for a maximum support.\r \r after some research across their own issues  https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/19197 , i took a look at the way  bootstrap  https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap  handle this  cc @cvrebert @mdo . here is the description of their sass  breakpoint-max  function.\r \r > maximum breakpoint width. null for the largest  last  breakpoint.\r > the maximum value is calculated as the minimum of the next one less 0.02px\r > to work around the limitations of  min-  and  max-  prefixes and viewports with > fractional widths.\r > see https://www.w3.org/tr/mediaqueries-4/ mq-min-max\r > uses 0.02px rather than 0.01px to work around a current rounding bug in safari.\r > see https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=178261\r \r so they use a precision of  0.02px , it would be something like  0.00125em  for us, which is close to the  0.001  proposed by @jasonmiller. i would agree to adopt this constant, still we need to do some body: there are two problems with geocoder/addresses in its interaction with the name autocompletion tools:\r single words aren't autocompleted, and single-word street name aliases are different than their official streetname which leads to confusion. \r \r for example, in the location services demo address tab, if you enter black, you get:\r    \r black bridge, kennedy lake, bc\r black creek bridge, black creek, bc\r black lane, tofino, bc\r black rd, black creek, bc\r    \r instead of\r    \r black bear tr 17 bridge, bc\r black creek bridge, black creek, bc\r black bear lane, tofino, bc\r black creek rd, black creek, bc\r    \r it was agreed that handling partial name matches in the parser is better than the current method of generating partial street and locality name aliases. in the past, handling partial name matches in the parser was ruled out because all the street centroids would have to be loaded which would be more trouble than it was worth. handling partial name matches in the parser makes address prep simpler because pseudo-aliases and centroids for pseudo-street aliases don't have to be generated. \r

title: handling keys in nav, and in sql server - something doesn't match here, and leads to strange phenomena.
body: as you know, nav allows up to 20 fields for sorting tables. this applies not only to the secondary keys  sk , to which the missing fields of the primary key are indirectly appended, but even more so to the actual primary key  pk .\r \r if the pk of a nav table has more than 16 fields, the error message \ record already exists\  may occur even though the nav logic of the pk is unique.\r \r example: the 17th field of the primary key is an integer field  e.g. entry no.  that is filled via the sql server  or also by the programming itself . if the first 16 fields are identical, this strange error message appears.\r \r this is because the sql server  at least sql server 2014  converts each key of a table into an index. but on the sql server itself such an index may have a maximum of 16 columns  = fields . this simply truncates the subsequent fields of the primary key  in the above case the integer field  and no longer belongs to the unique key on the sql side, which ultimately leads to the above error.\r \r this means that primary keys must already be unique in the first 16 fields. in the above example, the integer field should therefore be created as a 16th field at the latest. to what extent it still makes sense, the 17th, 18th, etc. field in the primary key is optional.

title: please add section on how to add ssl certificates to your application
body: https://github.com/jboss-openshift/application-templates the \ https configuration\  section.  and then the https://github.com/jboss-openshift/application-templates/tree/master/secrets for examples on how to insert the cert into the json.  here are the necessary steps: 1  create service account for eap:   create following json file  name it eap-sa.json : {     \ kind\ : \ serviceaccount\ ,     \ apiversion\ : \ v1\ ,     \ metadata\ : {         \ name\ : \ eap-service-account\      } } oc create -f eap-sa.json  2  generate keystore  example of generating self-signed certificate : keytool -genkey -keyalg rsa -alias selfsigned -keystore keystore.jks -storepass password -validity 360 -keysize 2048  answer the first question with full address of service, e.g. test.namespace.cloudapps.example.com   3  create secret from keystore: oc secrets new eap-secret keystore.jks  4  add secret to service account: oc secrets add serviceaccounts/deployer secrets/eap-secret  5  create application from template  e.g. eap6-basic-sti . make sure following variables are set: application_hostname  whatever you set to keystore  eap_https_secret=eap-secret  whatever you named your secret  eap_https_keystore=keystore.jks  whatever you named the keysotre  eap_https_name=selfsigned  whatever alias you set when creating certificate  eap_https_password=password  whatever you set when creating keystore   there are a few things to be aware of: - service account has to be named 'eap-service-account', otherwise deploymentconfig must be updated - there must be same password for certificate private key and for keystore  limitation of eap  - bold names can be changed, but the subsequent variables and commands have to be modified accordingly.

body: https://github.com/irungentoo/toxcore/blob/master/toxcore/net_crypto.c l1360\r \r if the realloc cant grow the region, it will allocate a second area of the requested size, copy everything over, free the old one,and return the new location back\r \r that will cause a copy of all shared_keys's to be left behind, and there is no safe way to clear them because malloc   may return the old ram to another thread\r \r the only solution i can see, is to allocate each crypto_connection seperately, and store an array of pointers to them\r \r the keys would also be protected more if that was done with sodium_malloc and sodium_free on the crypto_connection instances

essence of the problem is that if you have a multiple module configuration, and want to plan and apply a subset to more properly layer the deployment, it fails because modules you have not targeted title: add import with function renaming
body: cryptol currently support qualified imports to avoid function name clashes. for example, consider aes s-box and t-box specifications whose top-level encryption and decryption functions are named  aesencrypt  and  aesdecrypt , respectively.  when trying to prove equivalences of their specification, one can currently use cryptol qualified imports as follows:      // import aesencrypt and aesdecrypt in aes as qualified names aessbox::aesencrypt and aessbox::aesdecrypt import aes as aessbox aesencrypt, aesdecrypt   // import aesencrypt and aesdecrypt in aestbox as qualified names aestbox::aesencrypt and aestbox::aesdecrypt import aestbox as aestbox aesencrypt, aesdecrypt       another approach that would be nice to have is renaming the imported functions, as follows:      // import function aesencrypt and aesdecrypt in aes as top-level functions sboxencrypt and sboxdecrypt import aes aesencrypt => sboxencrypt, aesdecrypt => sboxdecrypt   // import function aesencrypt and aesdecrypt in aestbox as top-level functions tboxencrypt and tboxdecrypt import aestbox aesencrypt => tboxencrypt, aesdecrypt => tboxdecrypt       this way, one can use unqualified names to refer to the functions, which would be especially useful for long module names.

title: research feature flag libraries for elixir/phoenix
body: @crq and i have been discussing the minimal barrier for entry for contributing to remote retro, and something that's come up is the idea of atomic prs. folks don't have whole days or weeks to work on a story, so they end up wanting to merge a subset of a feature. how do we allow them to contribute their portion of a story without borking the repo?\r \r the two options that spring to mind are gitflow and feature flags. \r \r without dumping on gitflow, well... none of the current contributors seemed enthused about introducing the cognitive overhead...\r \r so what about feature flag libraries for elixir and/or react. this would allow us to merge in completed acceptance criteria piecemeal, waiting for all acceptance criteria to make its way into master before turning on the feature flag.

title: purpose of shoes-package
body: as i've started peeling away the layers around packaging, i'm having doubts about needing shoes-package  gem.\r \r current dependency tree:\r \r    \r shoes-swt\r -> shoes-package\r     -> furoshiki\r       -> warbler\r -> shoes-core\r    \r \r hints we've got an unnecessary split:\r \r   turns out, we aren't even using the  shoes::package::jar  and  shoes::package::jarapp  classes at all-- we're just using the  furoshiki  versions of them!  https://github.com/shoes/shoes4/blob/master/shoes-swt/lib/shoes/swt/packager.rb l72-l81 \r   despite  shoes-swt  depending on  shoes-package  gem-wise,  shoes-package  is  tightly bound to the swt backend  https://github.com/shoes/shoes4/blob/master/shoes-package/lib/warbler/traits/shoes.rb l34 \r   removing  shoes::package::jar  and  shoes::package::jarapp  leaves  shoes-package  with just the  shoes::package::configuration  class and warbler trait setup.\r   if there's generic packaging logic to share across backends, it belongs up in  shoes-core  with   shoes::packager   https://github.com/shoes/shoes4/blob/master/shoes-core/lib/shoes/packager.rb , not separated into yet another gem.\r \r what do you think of cleaning the cruft and hoisting those couple of bits up into a packager subdirectory in  shoes-swt ? @pragtob

title: incorrect indentation when closing hanging indent
body: if a hanging indent is closed after some values have been entered, it incorrectly keeps the indentation level.  example:      python x =       0,1,2,3       pressing enter before the     character results in      python x =       0,1,2,3            instead of producing      python x =       0,1,2,3        as expected. if the hanging indent were created to begin with, then the bracket would be correctly placed, this only occurs if a previously non-hanging-indented set of lines were converted to a hanging indent.  note, however, that it is _not_ enough simply to look for a comma. consider the case of the  admittedly rarely used  multi-line string created via parentheses:      python x =       'here is a multi-line string'     ' that spans several lines without any commas'     ' how will we detect this correctly? if this were'     ' inside brackets, then we would want to see if there'     ' is a comma, but since it is parentheses, there does'     ' not need to be a comma...'     'it appears as if there is no certain way to tell what the'     ' indentation should be here, probably best to default to'     ' current behavior, which is to set indentation to current indentation.'    x =       'compare the above to this',     'where now we should close the hanging'     'indent because there is no comma'        need to think more about what the desired behavior actually is here.

title: best operating system suggestion for hardware application
body: as per current prototype of susi hardware that has hotword detection and handsfree interaction, any operating system can be used for basic testing.\r but for final product, we must decide and focus our work on a particular flavor of linux, since it will help to maintain uniformity in project.\r \r    current options\r     raspbian  fork of debian \r   pros  \r - excellent support for raspberry pi development board.\r - most developers are familiar with debian.\r \r   cons  \r - focused on raspberry pi, ignores other development boards.\r - a lot of unneeded software preinstalled which uses ram in the background.  \r \r     ubuntu core\r   pros  \r - support for many development boards.\r - familiarity with debain\r \r   cons  \r - packages for voice tts festival which is being used is needed to be compiled manually,\r - voice packs for tts are needed to be installed manually,\r \r     arch linux for arm/ arch linux\r   pros  \r - minimal. no extra software by default. installation can be customized to suit our susi hardware apps specific needs.\r - support all development boards like orange pi, omega, raspberry pi\r - festival tts application is available on official repositories for all platforms  arm/x86/x64  with voice packages as well.  huge \r - fully packaged solution can be distributed using aur  https://aur.archlinux.org/  for installation as easy as a single line.  huge \r \r   cons  \r - unfamiliarity of some developers with arch environment.\r - relatively small community.\r - some different conventions from other operating systems like python3 as default and bleeding edge distribution  always latest version of all packages . \r \r \r \r this being said, i strongly recommend arch linux to be used to develop solution however i'm free to other opinions as well. \r

title: future::get   called from a thread may throw even though future is not yet unresolved
body: future::wait    may throw because  future::schedule    may throw. when that happens, the future will not be waited for. there are places we need to always wait for correctness, for example when waiting for all background operations to avoid use-after-free.\r \r the problem is similar to that described in commit 8f8cfe9f32deed1dc272bd91d9e8a4832d7cd180, and has the same cause. we should probably mark  future::wait    as noexcept.

title: mypy should not follow imports from stubs with --follow-imports=skip
body: currently, even with  --follow-imports=skip  imports from stub files are still followed. this means that if stub imports an unanalyzed module, the previously unanalyzed module is actually typechecked.\r \r consider the following example:\r    py\r   main.py\r from stub import x\r    \r \r    py\r   stub.pyi\r from unanalyzed import x\r    \r \r    py\r   unanalyzed.py\r x: int = 42\r \r x + ''    error is reported here but it shouldn't be because this file is unanalyzed\r    \r \r currently, if you run mypy the following happens:\r    \r $ mypy main.py --follow-imports=skip\r unanalyzed.py:4: error: unsupported operand types for +  \ int\  and \ str\  \r    \r \r i think we should treat imports from stub and non-stub files the same way. following imports from stubs in silent mode was implemented  1372.\r \r discovered this bug when investigation a reported error in dropbox internal codebases.

title: guest goals and alternate gameplay
body: right now our players have more motivation to control the guests near the end of the game  when they're hungry  than near the start of the game  when they're not . however one alternate gameplay mode which has been proposed is to have the players door start locked, and the guests to complete a number of objectives to unlock it, after which they're at risk of losing.\r \r this would come with a different introduction. the service kitchen has been placed into lockdown, but this can be overriden from locations around the hotel: the plant room, the office, a terminal in the library, etc.\r \r the players' door would have a number of lights  eg: 5  above it indicating the level of lock-down. we have a heartbeat that checks to see if guests are in one of the goal locations, and if so the number of lights goes down by one, and that location is crossed off the objectives list.\r \r this provides a constant pressure on the players to keep the guests out of certain areas. this becomes harder as more guests are moving, and combined with door decay   29  keeping a specific room locked down becomes increasingly challenging.\r \r from a coding standpoint, much of this is easy to add. we already have heartbeats with the plant room lockout. guests already have goal lists they execute, and which change with hunger. we're probably just adding a boolean to each room  is it a current goal  which gets cleared when it's completed. we can even have events which  add  rooms as goals, so players have to concentrate on more areas over time.\r \r the lights above the door simply require a driver of some sort and some code to display the number of locks remaining.\r \r it would be nice if current goals on the map were indicated visually somehow, perhaps by having an led  breathing  by adjusting its pwm values over time. we'd need to test this with the current event loop to see if it looks good or if there's noticeable lag during heavy cpu usage  eg: pathfinding .

title: building for windows documentation
body: i've been switching from using a vm to using the new ubuntu app built on windows subsystem for linux. this runs ubuntu 16.04.3 lts.\r \r following the current documentation at https://handbrake.fr/docs/en/latest/developer/build-windows.html revealed a couple of errors and perhaps deficiencies.\r \r     problems with dependencies\r \r      using a fresh installation, the quoted dependencies can't be installed without first issuing a  sudo apt-get update  command - otherwise  yasm  is not visible. it would be good practice to bring the installed system up-to-date at the same time i.e.  sudo apt-get upgrade && sudo apt autoremove  after the  update .\r \r       i think these commands should be included in the documentation\r \r      the actual list of dependencies doesn't include those needed to run the  mingw-w64-build  script. further packages needed, of those listed in the script as requirements, are  bison bzip2 flex g++ gunzip pax .\r \r      although  libtool  is listed as a dependency, it is not recognised by the configure script unless  libtool-bin  is also installed. although the script has facilities for building this  and  pkg-config   if missing, this didn't work for me.\r \r the sufficient dependencies to add to a fresh install that i found were  bison cmake curl flex g++ gcc git intltool libtool libtool-bin m4 make patch pax pkg-config python tar wget yasm .   some of these e.g.  git  are in fact installed in the released system. \r \r i think the list in the documentation should be updated.  the list for building for ubuntu at https://handbrake.fr/docs/en/latest/developer/install-dependencies-ubuntu.html provides another view - it doesn't include  pax  for example. \r \r i imagine these results would be the same in a fresh native install of ubuntu.\r     controlling the build\r \r the documentation gives no guidance on controlling the build.\r \r   for users wishing to build a release version of handbrake for example to include the fdk-aac encoder, i think a mention of the use of the git tag facility as used by handbrake should be included i.e.\r    \r     git tag  this lists the tags \r     git checkout tags/1.0.3  or whichever version you want from the list ,\r    \r       this allows the specific version of handbrake to be built.\r \r   similarly, the options available with configure aren't mentioned. the facility to list usage by calling  ./configure -h  might be included. in any case the specific case of building to include the fdk-aac encoder, i.e. the  --enable-fdk-aac  option, could be explicitly mentioned given that is probably a motivation for building your own\r \r     using windows filestore\r \r if the option of using the windows ubuntu app is documented, the following might also be noted.\r \r ms recommend using windows filestore  drvfs  for this sort of work i.e. placing the source somewhere in the regular windows user ntfs space and linking to this from the linux world, rather than cloning handbrake to  ~/handbrake . this has the advantage of being able to build the gui from the same clone as the dll, rather than maintaining two workspaces.  that was a reason for me to do this anyway. \r \r there are a couple of problems with this currently.\r \r      when using gnu tar to extract source, the original file times of the source files are not maintained. this plays havoc with subsequent attempts to make. i've raised a bug report with ms and they will eventually fix this. in the meantime, you can use the port of bsdtar from http://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/libarchive.htm by quoting the path e.g.  --gtar=/mnt/c/sw/gnuwin32/gnuwin32/bin/bsdtar.exe  to  configure .\r \r      also, there is some problem with using concurrency. the build works if make is not asked to run more than 1 job at a time i.e.  --launch-jobs=1  or a call of make without any options works. i've not tried to diagnose this - it may be a fault in the build system exposed by the different scheduling running against the windows linux kernel implementation.\r \r whether either of these issues ought to be documented in the handbrake build for windows documentation i don't know.\r \r i've only used a toolchain built-in linux filestore  volfs  i.e.  scripts/mingw-w64-build x86_64 ~/hbtoolchain \r     building using msys2\r \r for building for windows, an alternative to build from a single workspace is to use gcc from the msys2 environment. this isn't currently documented for handbrake and since the build system supports it, perhaps this ought to be documented here too.\r \r after installing msys2 from http://www.msys2.org/ and updating with\r \r    \r pacman -syu\r pacman -su\r    \r \r i added the following packages:\r \r    \r pacman -s base-devel cmake diffutils gcc git make mingw-w64-cross mingw-w64-cross-toolchain mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-x86_64-yasm yasm\r    \r \r and then ran\r \r    \r git clone https://github.com/handbrake/handbrake.git && cd handbrake\r ./configure --cross=x86_64-w64-mingw32 --enable-qsv --enable-fdk-aac --launch-jobs=10 --launch\r \r    \r this is all in an msys shell rather than a mingw64 shell - the latter fails in configure unable to find  x86_64-w64-mingw32-ar

title: reassigning and unset issues
body: i notice you reassign and unset the sensitive values. from what i can tell from memory dumps:\r - reassigning values does not overwrite the memory location the previous value was stored at but creates an entry at a new memory address. \r - also unset doesn't clear the memory so you can still see the previous content.  \r \r also depending on implementation and environment reassigning before performing unset might do more harm than good.\r \r is there a better way to clear these values from memory? i'm more of a c guy so it took me a while to even view the memory address and contents of shell script. let alone come up with a solution.

' 23:59:59';\r    \r \r we get the user's expiration date _formatted_. in this customer's case it was  23 january, 2018   note the comma .\r \r but  strtotime    doesn't like commas, so that final variable  $exp_date_dt  ended up being  2017-01-23 23:59:59  . the year got changed to  2017  instead of  2018  which killed the whole thing.\r \r this can easily be fixed by getting the unformatted expiration date instead.

title: search provider extension api
body: i looked into what it will take to run search in the extension host using extension apis.\r \r - ripgrep search\r     - just need to port ripgreptextsearch.ts and ripgrepfilesearch.ts\r     - currently it downloads the correct ripgrep binary at build time. a builtin extension in the core repo can still do that. a marketplace extension would have to ship all binaries and pick one at runtime.\r     - dependencies\r         - has lots of trivial dependencies from vs/base/common. it's ok to copy them, move to native node versions, or native es versions\r         - glob.ts, but we should get rid of that dependency. it's only used for sibling clauses and those should be handled on the frontend\r     - api\r         - doesn't expose all features that builtin search needs\r             - whether to use gitignore file\r             - follow symlinks\r             - max filesize\r             - encoding  can be read from files.encoding, do we expect all \r extension authors to think of that? \r             - result limit count  handled by frontend using cancellationtoken? \r         \t- searching outside of the workspace\r \t\t\t- smart case  front end \r \t\t\t- wordseparators  front end \r             - cache search  for file search \r             - sort by score  for file search \r \t\t\t- multiroot search  change it to search per single folder \r         - need to read relativepattern, instead of the current ifolderquery\r     - logging\r         - use extensionhost logger and output pane\r     - frontend changes - searchservice just need to talk to search provider api\r - non-rg search is harder\r     - need glob.ts, and all of its dependencies\r     - mime\r     - iconv and the stuff we have built around it\r     - ipc stuff from core for spawning worker processes\r     - all of the dependencies would have to be moved to a separate node module so they can be shared with search. we probably don't want to do that.\r \r

title: reset session's state in case of activation failure
body: the problem\r \r current  powerauthsdk  implementations doesn't handle internal session's state properly during the activation process. we're forcing developers to reset the sdk object state before the activation or in case of error. all this situations should be handled in the sdk internally and the sdk behavior should be more predictable. \r \r    solution\r \r it looks like that we have to just add reset the session at various error points during the activation, but that's not true. the problem is more complex as it looks like at first sight : \r \r 1. remove  powerauthsdk.reset    method. the method has a confusing naming and very unclear implementation.  \r 2. add  powerauthsdk.cancelpendingactivation    method with a similar functionality to removed  reset   . unlike the  reset   , this new method will be allowed only during the activation process and should properly cancel possible network communication.\r 3. make sure, that cancelling a pending asynchronous task returned from  createactivation... will also notify sdk about that cancellation. it's expected that developer can use both ways  cancelling the task or cancelling the pending activation in genera, via the sdk methodl \r 4. make sure, that an error during the activation process always leads to an empty session. \r

title: resumption should listen on all the choices simultaniously

body: currently it is impossible to use wskdeploy to  deploy ow assets  action, package...etc  of the same signature from different manifests having different project names. the problem is that wskdeploy overrides the \ managed project\  annotation. the workaround could be to use different package names, which results in assets duplication. duplication is undesirable, because it complicates maintenance. \r introducing a feature allowing to manage ow assets by multiple projects would help to avoid it.\r suggestion:\r - use different annotation key instead of \ manage\  for the sake of backward compatibility. e.g.  managedlist  holding an array of managed project names.\r - on manifest deployment, if a deployed asset already exists in ow, check whether the manifest asset is identical to the existing one.\r if not: override the existing asset with the manifest one  similar to the current functionality \r if yes: add the project specified in the manifest to the  managedlist .

title: is there a path towards less fragmented code / less scattered semantic content?
body: in a code review today, @klindsay28 pointed out that semantic content that is only needed in  interior_tendency_compute    may be spread out among several modules. for example, if you want to add a new class of dissolved organic matter you need to update  dissolved_organic_matter_type  in  marbl_interface_private_types.f90  and  store_diagnostics_dissolved_organic_matter    in  marbl_diagnostics_mod.f90 . while the code design for marbl 1.0.0 is pretty locked in place, some things to think about for marbl 2.0  and beyond :\r \r 1. right now marbl is built on a principle of keeping semantic content out of the gcm as much as possible - can that be extended to only keep semantic content in specific marbl modules? i.e. could we replace most of the datatypes in  marbl_interface_private_types.f90  with flat arrays and let  init  build up indexing types?  would this help the scattered content, or just replace existing private datatypes with indexing types? \r 1. could we auto-generate  marbl_interface_private_types.f90   maybe from a yaml / json dictionary that defines the various data types? \r 1. are there other ways to auto-generate code that would allow developers to use semantic content in  marbl_interior_tendency_mod.f90.template  and then somehow auto-generate private types, the actual interior tendency module, etc?

title: matrixobj: define and implement semantics for comparing matrixobj and vectorobj
body: one of the problems with treating matrices and vectors like lists is that we have to adopt the rules for comparing lists; and two lists are equal if they have equal elements. this means that all 0-dimensional vectors and matrices over all base domains should be equal, at least as long as they are lists.\r \r to resolve that, we want to have matrixobj and vectorobj implementations which are not lists  see also  2148 . but then we should still define precise semantics as to when two vectors or two matrices compare as equal. here is a first suggestion for how that might work:\r   a vectorobj and a matrixobj are never equal\r   two vectorbj are equal if they ...\r     have equal length,\r     have \ compatible\  base domains,\r     contain equal elements\r   two matrixobj are equal if they ...\r     have equal numbers of rows,\r     have equal number of columns,\r     have \ compatible\  base domains,\r     contain equal elements\r \r this leaves the question what constitutes \ compatible\  base domains. a simple but overly restrict definition would be to require the base domains to be equal.\r \r this solves some problems, but would be a radical departure from how vectors in gap\r currently work, and i think that alone makes it a bad choice. there is also the matter of inconvenience caused by this when writing code.\r \r another definition would be to say two base domains are \ compatible\  if one is \ contained\  in the other, with compatible structure  i.e. addition/multiplication/subtraction of the \ larger\  base domain restrict to those of the \ smaller\  one.\r \r so for fields, that just means they are compatible if one is a subfield of the other, which matches what we do right now, i think.\r \r the one thing i am a bit worried here is whether we can tests this efficiently, i.e., i don't want risk introducing a bottleneck here.\r \r therefore, we might want to use a slightly different definition:\r   a vectorobj and a matrixobj are never equal\r   two vectorbj are equal if they ...\r     have equal length,\r     contain equal elements,\r     and, if they are empty, then they must have \ compatible\  base domains.\r   two matrixobj are equal if they ...\r     have equal numbers of rows,\r     have equal number of columns,\r     have \ compatible\  base domains,\r     contain equal elements\r     and, if they are empty, then they must have \ compatible\  base domains.\r \r this way, we only need to compare the base domains for empty vectors and matrices, which should be relatively rare. drawback: it is a little bit less flexible. e.g. with the former model, people could write special \ strict\  base domains, which are not compatible with any other base domain, to get some kind of \ strict typing\  through the backdoor. not sure if that's a good idea to start with, but i wanted to mention it for completeness.\r \r \r as to how to implement testing for compatibility of base domains, i'd try to use method dispatch for that, to make it extensible:\r \r    gap\r declareoperation \ iscompatiblebasedomain\ ,  isobject, isobject  ;\r \r   identical base domains are always compatible\r installmethod iscompatiblebasedomain, isidenticalobj,  isobject, isobject , sum_flags,\r function bd1, bd2 \r     if isidenticalobj bd1, bd2  then return true; fi;\r     trynextmethod  ;\r end ;\r \r   fallback: if no method fired, then assume the base domains are not compatible\r installmethod iscompatiblebasedomain,\r      isobject, isobject ,\r     returnfalse ;\r \r   cyclotomics are always compatible\r installmethod iscompatiblebasedomain, isidenticalobj,\r      iscyclotomiccollection, iscyclotomiccollection ,\r     returntrue ;\r \r   ffe domains are compatible if they have equal characteristic\r installmethod iscompatiblebasedomain, isidenticalobj,\r      isffecollection, isffecollection ,\r     {bd1, bd2} -> characteristic bd1  = characteristic bd2  ;\r    \r
